q: Does the paper's non-abelian HSP extension (Section 6, requiring a strongly complementary pair with a normal-classical-states property on the group observable) yield a concrete Hilbert-space instantiation for any non-abelian group of interest --- e.g. the dihedral group D_n, relevant to lattice cryptography via Regev's reduction?
basis: The paper only shows the abstract diagrammatic proof goes through with the extra assumption that all classical states of the group observable are normal, but does not exhibit any Hilbert-space example. Our replication is restricted to abelian G (Z_8 and Z_15) because the concrete non-abelian instantiation is absent from the paper.
next_steps: For D_3, D_4, and Q_8, construct the standard group algebra C[G] with its regular representation, ask numerically whether any pair of dagger-Frobenius algebras on C[G] (one point structure, one group structure) satisfies both strong complementarity AND the paper's Section-6 normality condition on classical states, and if so, whether the paper's five-step rewrite chain reproduces the standard non-abelian HSP output statistics on that instantiation.

q: Does the paper's Section 5.7 isometry-cancellation rewrite (s^dagger s = id, dropping the classical outcome b from the register-1 marginal) compile into a mechanical ZX-diagram rewrite sequence, and if so, does PyZX or QuiZX full_reduce reach the target normal form (Diagram 5.3 RHS) within a bounded number of steps for our specific test groups Z_8 and Z_15?
basis: Our V3 check verified the isometry-cancellation rewrite numerically for 10 random hiding functions (both pipelines gave identical register-1 marginals to ~1e-16), but numerical equality is a strictly weaker check than an actual diagrammatic execution of the rewrite chain. Whether the ZX rewriter used by tools like PyZX can EXECUTE Gogioso and Kissinger's proof (not just verify one instance of one step) is an open question.
next_steps: Encode the coherent oracle U_f for Z_8 with H=<2> as a ZX diagram using PyZX green/red spider primitives, encode the input state, execute PyZX's full_reduce and simp routines, and check whether the output diagram simplifies to a green H^perp-supported label spider (i.e. Diagram 5.3 RHS). Repeat for Z_15 with H=<5>. Report the step-count and success/failure of the automated simplification.

q: For our two test groups, we chose hiding function labels via uniformly random injection of cosets into Z_2^M. The paper's proof is symbolic and should hold for every valid hiding function, but is there a class of adversarial label choices (e.g. Gray-code-permuted labels, high-Hamming-weight labels, labels that concentrate on a subset of Z_2^M) that induces detectable numerical deviation from uniform-on-H^perp at larger |G|, or is the uniform-on-H^perp output truly label-independent to machine precision?
basis: Our V3 sweep across 5 random hiding functions per test group returned max deviation < 3e-16 --- perfect within float64 noise. This is consistent with the paper's proof (which never depends on the specific label choice, only on the coset-preserving-and-injective property), but our sample size is small.
next_steps: Enumerate all (|G/H|!) valid label permutations for Z_8 with H=<2> (i.e. 2! = 2 permutations, trivial) and Z_15 with H=<5> (5! = 120 permutations), run the full pipeline on each, and report the max L2 deviation of the register-1 marginal from uniform-on-H^perp. If deviation is < 1e-14 for all permutations, promote to Z_16 with H=<4> (4! = 24) and Z_24 with H=<8> (3! = 6). If some permutation triggers > 1e-10, examine QFT numerical stability.

q: The paper's Diagram 5.3 gives the FULL joint (b, chi) probability as |H|^2 / |G|^2 for (b, chi) in im(s) x Ann[H]. We verified this indirectly via the character marginal and per-coset conditionals; how does the register-2 marginal P(b) behave? Does it exactly match |H|/|G| per coset (uniform over image of s) in our runs, and does the joint (y, b) distribution factorise as P(y|b) P(b) with P(y|b) constant in b (as Diagram 5.3 asserts)?
basis: We computed the full joint matrix |A[y,b]|^2 (of shape N x 2^M) but only reported the register-1 marginal and per-coset conditionals; the register-2 marginal and factorisation property were verified only via the qualitative 'all coset conditionals identical' flag.
next_steps: For both test groups, extract and print the register-2 marginal P(b) for every b in {0,...,2^M-1}, compare to the analytic value |H|/|G| = 4/8 = 0.5 (Z_8) and 3/15 = 0.2 (Z_15) for b in image(s), and verify P(b) = 0 for b not in image(s). Then check the L2 deviation from the analytic factorisation P(y,b) = P(y) P(b) < 1e-15.

q: The concrete instantiation used the standard QFT_N with sign convention omega = exp(+2*pi*i/N). For cyclic Z_N, H^perp is symmetric under sign flip, so the choice does not affect our support-checks. The paper's diagrammatic proof uses the group algebra's antipode to define the character basis; is the sign convention fixed by the antipode choice, or is it convention-free, and does the choice matter for direct products such as Z_{n_1} x Z_{n_2} where H^perp may not be sign-symmetric?
basis: Our tests are all cyclic; we never observed a discrepancy that could be attributed to sign convention. But the paper's non-cyclic-abelian case (e.g. Z_2 x Z_4) is not tested here and could expose the issue.
next_steps: Run the full pipeline on G = Z_2 x Z_4 with H = <(1,0)> and with H = <(0,2)>, using both sign conventions of the QFT_G, and check whether the sampled character y = (y_1, y_2) lies in H^perp for both conventions. If the two conventions produce different H^perp supports, trace which one matches the paper's diagrammatic antipode definition.
